You are making the decision of the participant described below in an anonymous money allocation activity. Use the rules and information given, and return only the signed number of tokens chosen, without an explanation.
You are randomly paired with another research participant. One person is Player A and the other is Player B. Each starts with 10 tokens, so the pair has 20 tokens. Twenty tokens are worth RMB10: each token is worth RMB0.50. Player A alone decides how many tokens to give to or take from Player B. Player A may give all, some or none of their own 10 tokens, or take all, some or none of Player B's 10 tokens. Player B makes no decision and cannot reject the allocation. This is one allocation decision, with no earlier allocation decisions in this activity. The examples below explain the rules; they are not your past choices.
Your response is a signed amount t between -10 and 10 inclusive. Negative t gives |t| tokens to B; positive t takes t tokens from B; t=0 neither gives nor takes. A ends with 10+t tokens and B with 10-t tokens. Thus t=-10 leaves A0 and B20; t=10 leaves A20 and B0. Each person's activity bonus equals their final tokens times RMB0.50. The activity bonus can range from RMB0 to RMB10. Completing the survey also earns a separate RMB5 participation payment, to be reviewed and paid within three days; the activity bonus is paid within seven days. The participation payment is additional to the activity bonus. No lottery or randomly selected round is involved in this one decision.
Before proceeding, the instructions ask four comprehension questions, all of which must be answered correctly to continue: (1) Whose decision determines both players' earnings? Options: A; B; both; cannot determine. (2) When does A earn most? Options: A does nothing; A takes all B's tokens; A gives all tokens to B; depends on B. (3) If A gives10, how many tokens does A earn? Options0,5,10,15,20. (4) If A takes5, how many tokens does A earn? Options0,5,10,15,20. These are comprehension checks rather than additional allocation choices. No personal attempt history is supplied.
The personal background below reports the same participant's established facts and experiences. Use only supplied values; an omitted field does not mean No. Birth year is not an exact age. Education may include a programme still in progress. Income intervals are current monthly RMB intervals, not annual income or interval midpoints. Household registration means hukou. The current province/city label is kept in its original proper-name spelling. Abroad for at least half a year includes exactly half a year; domestic residence outside the hukou city uses at least one year. Ever smoked does not imply current smoking. Vaccination means at least one dose, not completion of a course. The past-month testing question concerns universal COVID19 nucleic-acid testing.
The original diagnosis question lists cardiovascular/cerebrovascular disease, chronic lung disease, diabetes, chronic liver disease, chronic kidney disease, tumours, an immune-compromised condition, and obesity. Its single yes/no response says whether a doctor ever diagnosed at least one listed condition; it does not identify a specific condition or individual medical risk. The original industry question lists imported cold-chain work, port quarantine, ship crews, air crews, fresh markets, public transportation, and medical/disease-control work. Its single yes/no response refers to employment in at least one listed industry. A report of being told one is vulnerable to COVID19 records that past communication, not a medical diagnosis. Cancellation/missed-occasion/told-vulnerable fields are supplied only when explicitly checked affirmative; missing flags are not negative answers. Network counts are the original brackets0,1,2-5,6+ and do not identify named people.

A takes3tokens from B: A finishes with13tokens and B with7tokens.

A neither gives nor takes: A finishes with10tokens and B with10tokens.

B answered: "Outside China." B returned to China in November2020.

Before the activity you read the following information and two comprehension questions. You may continue only after answering both correctly.
As of21September2021, the WHO had received reports of228,807,631 confirmed COVID19 cases worldwide, including4,697,099 deaths. To reduce cross-border spread, Chinese citizens abroad must apply to the local Chinese embassy for a green health code before returning to China. Before boarding they must obtain a double-negative certificate from a designated or approved testing institution, with sampling and testing within48hours before boarding. This requires (1) a negative nucleic-acid test using nasal/pharyngeal swabs and (2) a negative serum-specific IgM antibody test using venous blood. Embassies generally require the report to explicitly identify serum, IgM, antibody and venous blood. Other sampling or testing, including fingertip blood and rapid testing, is not accepted. Embassy requirements vary, but double-negative certification is a necessary condition for boarding. Many embassies further require cross-double testing: multiple nasal/pharyngeal swabs and venous-blood sampling to obtain two double-negative certificates. Some also require pre-boarding isolation and health monitoring, for example self-isolation and health monitoring during the14days before boarding. Testing procedures and designated agencies have repeatedly changed and may change at any time. Upon arrival in China, airport nucleic-acid testing is followed by closed-loop transport directly to designated, self-financed centralised quarantine for14days, during which multiple nucleic-acid tests are administered.
Question1: How is an IgM antibody test sampled? Saliva; fingertip blood; venous blood; all of the above. Question2: Some embassies require cross-double testing involving multiple nasal/pharyngeal swabs and venous-blood sampling. Correct; incorrect; cannot determine from the text.

This requires (1) a negative nucleic-acid test using nasal/pharyngeal swabs and (2) a negative serum-specific IgM antibody test using venous blood. Before boarding they must obtain a double-negative certificate from a designated or approved testing institution, with sampling and testing within48hours before boarding. This requires (1) a negative nucleic-acid test using nasal/pharyngeal swabs and (2) a negative serum-specific IgM antibody test using venous blood. Upon arrival in China, airport nucleic-acid testing is followed by closed-loop transport directly to designated, self-financed centralised quarantine for14days, during which multiple nucleic-acid tests are administered.

Testing procedures and designated agencies have repeatedly changed and may change at any time. Upon arrival in China, airport nucleic-acid testing is followed by closed-loop transport directly to designated, self-financed centralised quarantine for14days, during which multiple nucleic-acid tests are administered.

As of21September2021, the WHO had received reports of228,807,631 confirmed COVID19 cases worldwide, including4,697,099 deaths. To reduce cross-border spread, Chinese citizens abroad must apply to the local Chinese embassy for a green health code before returning to China. Before boarding they must obtain a double-negative certificate from a designated or approved testing institution, with sampling and testing within48hours before boarding. This requires (1) a negative nucleic-acid test using nasal/pharyngeal swabs and (2) a negative serum-specific IgM antibody test using venous blood. Embassies generally require the report to explicitly identify serum, IgM, antibody and venous blood. Other sampling or testing, including fingertip blood and rapid testing, is not accepted. Embassy requirements vary, but double-negative certification is a necessary condition for boarding. Many embassies further require cross-double testing: multiple nasal/pharyngeal swabs and venous-blood sampling to obtain two double-negative certificates. As of21September2021, the WHO had received reports of228,807,631 confirmed COVID19 cases worldwide, including4,697,099 deaths. Before boarding they must obtain a double-negative certificate from a designated or approved testing institution, with sampling and testing within48hours before boarding. This requires (1) a negative nucleic-acid test using nasal/pharyngeal swabs and (2) a negative serum-specific IgM antibody test using venous blood. Upon arrival in China, airport nucleic-acid testing is followed by closed-loop transport directly to designated, self-financed centralised quarantine for14days, during which multiple nucleic-acid tests are administered.

Before boarding they must obtain a double-negative certificate from a designated or approved testing institution, with sampling and testing within48hours before boarding. This requires (1) a negative nucleic-acid test using nasal/pharyngeal swabs and (2) a negative serum-specific IgM antibody test using venous blood. Embassy requirements vary, but double-negative certification is a necessary condition for boarding. Before boarding they must obtain a double-negative certificate from a designated or approved testing institution, with sampling and testing within48hours before boarding. This requires (1) a negative nucleic-acid test using nasal/pharyngeal swabs and (2) a negative serum-specific IgM antibody test using venous blood. Before boarding they must obtain a double-negative certificate from a designated or approved testing institution, with sampling and testing within48hours before boarding. This requires (1) a negative nucleic-acid test using nasal/pharyngeal swabs and (2) a negative serum-specific IgM antibody test using venous blood. Embassies generally require the report to explicitly identify serum, IgM, antibody and venous blood. Other sampling or testing, including fingertip blood and rapid testing, is not accepted. Embassy requirements vary, but double-negative certification is a necessary condition for boarding. Many embassies further require cross-double testing: multiple nasal/pharyngeal swabs and venous-blood sampling to obtain two double-negative certificates.
